Commentary.Commentary: That brings down the curtains to the league matches. We have got the second team who will enter the finals, it's the West Indies and boy, have they romped through in some style. On 26th June, 2016 we will bring you the coverage of the final game between West Indies and Australia at the same venue at 2230 IST. Should be a cracker of a game. Until next time, goodbye and take care! Cheers!

Man of the Match, Darren Bravo says that earlier in the series he was disappointed about getting out after starts. However, he says he played very well in the nets yesterday and went in with a positive mindset this time. He claims his partnership with Kieron Pollard was a great one as he matched him ball-for-ball. He feels that Rabada bowled very well and is one of the fastest bowlers he has faced. He wishes him the best and says that the hosts executed their game plan well. He feels that the support of the crowd goes a long way and hopes folks will come see them play on Sunday as they face the best team in the world and will be sticking to their game plan.

West Indies skipper, Jason Holder says he is really happy with the win and is very proud of his boys. Adds this win was important for West Indies cricket. Continues by praising the efforts of Bravo and Pollard as that helped them come back in the game. Admits they were under pressure early on but is proud of the way Bravo kept the fight going. On Shannon Gabriel, he says he is a superb bowler and bowls with great pace. He says, they just told him to inject life in the game. Ends up saying Australia are a tough opponent and they are the World Champions for a reason. His team is aware that if they have to give a fight, they will have to bring their 'A' game.

South African captain, AB de Villiers says that his side was off to fantastic start and had a couple of opportunities to run through the hosts but stumbled at those moments. He feels that it was a great opportunity to pick up the 5th and 6th wickets and that those scalps would have changed everything. He was irritated with the discipline, the extras given, especially the wides and fumbles on the field. He says that it was a fantastic knock by Bravo and gives him credit. He talks about the series and says that they won a couple of games to stay in the series and is overall disappointed with their performance in this series.

Shannon Gabriel might have dropped a catch but followed next with three scalps in his five overs early into the game. Holder overcame his hamstring injury to bowl all 10 overs. Earlier in the day, West Indies made a remarkable comeback to set a noteworthy total and they have truly exceeded expectations whether they win or they lose in the finals. Stay tuned for the post-match presentation.

Each of the Windies bowlers returned impeccable figues at the end of the day, complimenting their superb fielding.The West Indians showed great discipline in their bowling early on, offering few extras and restricting the batsmen, with their fielders staying alert and picking up several catches and stopping the flow of runs. However, all that changed in the death overs as they let runs seep through and displayed some careless fielding. Sunil Narine was the star of the bowling attack, taking three big wickets and restricting the batsmen from scoring the runs.

Behardien managed to anchor the innings for a while, putting up 35 runs from 57 balls, the top scorer for the visitors. His partnership with Parnell lasted for 59 balls but he was soon caught out by Charles. Things looked nigh impossible for South Africa at this point but Parnell stuck on, to stubbornly bring up 28 runs until he was caught out by Carter. Picking up where he left off, Morne Morkel and Imran Tahir brought up the highest partnership of the innings, raising a glimmer of hope. But it was a little too late.

The batsmen were dismissed steadily throughout the innings and there was a marked absence of fireworks. Amla and de Kock opened the innings but were unable to create much of an impact. de Kock was dismissed after facing only six balls and Faf du Plessis followed soon after. The cheap wickets continued when Gabriel picked up the scalp of AB de Villiers for 2.

It's curtains for the Proteas! West Indies demolish the South African batting line-up to make it into the finals of the tri-series against Australia! A hugely disappointing response from the Proteas to the West Indian innings. Note - This is the first time since 2005-06, South Africa have failed to make it to the finals of a tri-series.
